articleTitle: The development of on-line thermal performance monitors in Nuclear Electric Company's stations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: The authors examine the benefits of using online monitoring techniques in assisting power station staff with the task of optimising the efficient use of reactor fuel. The role of thermal performance monitoring for detecting changes in plant conditions is examined and the way in which the data can be used by engineers to assist with the preparation of operating and maintenance programmes also discussed. To reduce the requirement for regular calibrations, an automatic software signal verification program is developed for use in online monitoring schemes. It forms part of the total unit performance calculation package and uses a whole plant model to verify plant signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

IEEE Keywords: Fission reactor cooling and heat recovery

articleTitle: Remote monitoring and processing of large quantities of on-line vibration data by an expert system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: Vibration monitoring of large turbine generators has been carried out by the power industry for many years, initiated by shaft cracking problems in the early 1970s. A system for collecting data from several on-line vibration monitoring systems is explained. The large amounts of data has necessitated the use of automatic screening programmes to detect any changes at the earliest possible moment without using excessive manpower. Several techniques for screening the data are presented which all show significant advantages in reducing the visual inspection of data although each have their associated disadvantages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PSAD, a new tool for condition monitoring of large component in EDF power plant
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: Electricite de France (EDF), like many utilities of major countries, looks for ways to improve availability and safety of its nuclear units. PSAD is an on-line monitoring system which provides plant personnel and experts with an efficient and user-friendly aid in decision making for the detection of failures occurring on the main components of nuclear power stations. It has a flexible architecture so it can accept both existing and new monitoring functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

IEEE Keywords: Fission reactor cooling and heat recovery

articleTitle: Performance data monitoring and analysis at Roosecote power station
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: The authors look at the performance data management tool (P-DAMAT) which is being installed at the Roosecote power station. It uses actual performance data and actual plant conditions to carry out a predictive performance analysis. P-DAMAT can be used to improve availability and efficiency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A user friendly simulation support environment for turbo generator defect diagnosis
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: The author describes work done in building a set of support tools for analysis using simulation software to diagnose turbogenerator faults. SPAR is a suite of five rotor dynamics programs designed to simulate the response of turbogenerators to a range of physical faults. The system described is essentially complete except for the elements involving machine learning, these are under development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced condition monitoring and fault diagnosis of turbo-alternators using an embedded expert system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: The authors discuss a monitoring and diagnostic embedded expert system (MODEES) which forms part of a more general condition monitoring and fault diagnosis system (COMFAD). This is a rule based system with the ability to categorise power plant performance and recognise impending failure or dangerous trending, and the need for preventative maintenance or remedial action. COMFAD/MODEES is targeted at operator personnel who must decide within a short period if the power plant is fit for continued or prolonged service, and if not make a thoroughly reasoned 'guess' at what faults have occurred and how they can be remedied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A data processing technique for steam turbines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: The author describes an application of state estimation techniques to the power plant steam turbines as an alternative to computers. The steam turbine state estimator is applied to a 250 MW, double flow, single-reheat cross-compound steam turbine with seven feedwater heaters. The turbine system has 18 state variables. The state estimator is tested under a wide range of measurement noises and measurement redundancy ratio (measurement redundancy ratio is defined as the ratio of the number of measurements to that of the number of state variables). Results show the state estimator significantly improves the measurement accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An on-line vibration monitoring system for power generating turbines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: It has been demonstrated that investment in equipment to monitor the state of health of the machinery can reduce down time, improve efficiency and enhance safety, thus producing great economic benefits. The author concentrates on a fundamental preliminary step, namely the acquisition of accurate and reliable measurements from the plant. The system described consists of a set of vibration measuring instruments coupled to a computer for the processing and display of the data. The system has been in use in UK power stations for a number of years and has achieved excellent results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rotordynamic modelling for turbogenerator defect diagnosis
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Advanced Condition Monitoring Systems for Power Generation
abstract: Defects in turbine rotors such as unbalances, bends, cracks and instabilities are diagnosed by the use of computer programs for rotordynamic modelling and by gathering together and validating data describing the shaft lines, oil film bearings and structural components of the relevant turbogenerators. The computer programs are based on those originally developed (Thomas 1972) and used for design calculations with only limited opportunities for experimental checks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
